purpose: Distinguish an abrupt steering-gauge boundary from a genuine smooth angle migration before applying centroid bias transport

bootstrap_features.aoa_step_consistency: robust median and MAD of per-slot |u_t-u_{t-1}| over t=1..19
bootstrap_features.slope_curvature: linear slope and residual curvature of u_t over first 20 outputs

provisional_decision_rule.gauge_boundary_candidate: gauge_rms>=0.10 rad AND phase_rms>=0.10 rad AND residual_gauge_corr>=0.70
provisional_decision_rule.tracked_or_settled_geometry_change: gauge_rms>=0.10 rad AND phase_rms<0.10 rad; do not transport
provisional_decision_rule.ambiguous: otherwise; abstain from transport and retain raw phase
provisional_decision_rule.threshold_status: provisional engineering diagnostic, not fitted or validated

offline_separability_observed: Full-horizon proxies separate post_200 (gauge~0.42, phase~0.42) from angle_migration (gauge~0.44, phase~0.045) and stable/pre_window (phase~0.01); first-20 AoA/correlation features were not persisted, so this is not a classifier result.
failure_boundaries: A ramp completed before bootstrap (pre_window) is indistinguishable from a settled geometry change using first-window residual alone.
Target-specific angle migration or target association changes can mix gauge and physical angle effects.
Large AoA noise, phase wraps, or missing slots can make residual_gauge_corr undefined.
A real motion-induced phase change can correlate with geometry by coincidence; no truth input may resolve that.
next_minimal_recording: Persist first-20 per-slot u_t, phase_residual_t, gauge_prediction_t, robust slope/MAD and correlation; then evaluate rule without truth.
